subject: Re: Summit Analytics — renewal pricing & staged uplift plan
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@summit-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@summit-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing conversation — Summit Analytics

Karthik,

Our agreement is up in May and the Procurement team asked me to open a pricing conversation early. Usage spiked this quarter as we onboarded two new product lines, and the finance team is focused on predictable unit economics.

High level asks from our side:
- Hold existing rate for first 12 months of renewal (price hold)
- Allow a 2-quarter staged commit uplift (start at current commit, move to +30% in Q2, +60% in Q3)
- One-time credit to offset historical overage incurred during onboarding (Q1 overages)

Can you confirm if Redwood can offer a structured path like the above? If helpful, I can share usage exports and calendar for a short call.

Thanks,
Claire Nguyen
Head of Procurement
Summit Analytics

Subject: Re: Renewal pricing conversation — Summit Analytics

Claire —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sending the usage snapshot. Quick read-through looks good; I can propose a package that maps to what you described. High level I can offer:
- 12-month price hold on current unit rates if Summit commits to a minimum 12-month term (no retroactive price resets)
- Staged commit uplift plan with explicit capacity targets per quarter and an automatic billing cadence to match the ramp
- One-time onboarding credit to offset Q1 overages (we typically amortize credits across the first invoice after renewal)

Before I pull together numbers I want to loop in Monica (CS) to validate the usage profile and Aditya (SE) to confirm capacity/throughput implications for the proposed commit increases.

Propose a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk the numbers and agree on the mutual action plan. If that works I’ll send an invite and a simple 1-page term summary.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the export. I reviewed the CSV and pulled a short usage summary (attached) that shows token volumes by model family and peak QPS windows. A few quick observations:

- There is a clear opportunity to realize savings by pinning a quantized variant for some high-volume routings and enabling prefix caching on predictable pipelines.

Claire —

Quick follow from the call earlier: technical feasibility for the staged uplift is solid. Two notes to align on cost modeling:
1) If you keep the same model mix we used in Q1, the effective unit cost at +60% commit will be ~12% lower than on-demand due to batching and KV cache improvements at scale.
2) If you switch 40% of traffic to our quantized-compatible variants we can materially reduce token cost; that requires a 2-week validation window and a controlled canary (we can do this within your sandbox).

I attached a simple spreadsheet with three scenarios: conservative (no quant), hybrid (40% quant), and aggressive (60% quant). It includes suggested commit thresholds and the credit math to offset Q1 overages.

Let me know which scenario you want priced and I’ll convert to an amortized monthly credit and roll into the Term Sheet.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer

Thanks for the quick turn. A few follow-ups from our finance side:
- We appreciate the price hold offer but need the hold guaranteed for 12 months from the renewal effective date (not just a billing cadence). Can you put that in writing?
- For the staged commit we want clear breakpoints and an opt-out clause if usage does not ramp to agreed levels after two quarters.
- On credits: procurement prefers a single one-off credit applied to the first renewal invoice rather than amortized credits over months.

Operational ask: can you provide a one-page term summary and a draft SOW so our legal can start the review in parallel? That will speed procurement.

Claire / Jordan —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise 1-page term summary and a draft SOW for your legal team. Key points from our side:
- 12-month firm price hold starting on the renewal effective date (we will capture this language in the amendment)
- Staged commit ladder: Q1 (baseline), Q2 +30% commit, Q3 +60% commit. Each step has a 45-day verification window; if usage does not reach the agreed threshold after two quarters, Summit can revert to baseline with no penalty (we will include an opt-out provision).
- One-time credit equals the Q1 measured overage up to a cap (see SOW appendix). Per your preference we’ll apply as a single credit on the first renewal invoice.
- Requested validation: 14-day quantization pilot for up to 40% traffic; success criteria are documented in SOW.

Next steps: I’ll queue a formal amendment and SOW in DocuSign once you confirm acceptance of the term summary. I’ve also linked the HubSpot deal (see link) for tracking and will ask Marissa (RevOps) to prepare a billing schedule aligned with your procurement milestones.

Proposed calendar: review legal comments week of Mar 15, sign by Mar 25 to allow for May renewal effective date.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
